sources.title: Michael Witzel, The Brahmins of Kashmir (1995; manuscript dated September 1991)
sources.note: Scholarly historical research. Original indexed PDF excerpts verified for Karkota section, corrected chronology beginning circa 625/626, Lalitaditya from 725, dynastic lists and Utpala succession 856. Direct PDF retrieval returned an HTML challenge; indexed original text was read. No territorial maximum inferred from Kalhana.

sources.title: Ved Kumari Ghai, The Nilamata Purana: A Brief Survey
sources.note: Scholarly editor and translator on a community-hosted page. Date discussion places core in sixth to eighth centuries, with subsequent additions after ninth/tenth. Prescriptive text is not statistical evidence of universal customs or social equality. Counted with other Nilamata-derived prose as one work.

sources.title: Nilamata Purana, Ved Kumari Ghai translation, verses 401 to 500
sources.note: Primary religious text in scholarly translation. Verses 407 to 420 household fires, lamps, decorated shops and family meals; 477 to 484 snowfall and cloaks. Prescriptions, not a diary. Combined with all other Nilamata material for source budget.

sources.title: Nilastotram, Sanskrit text of the hymn to Nila
sources.note: Modern Devanagari transcription of primary Sanskrit hymn, proofread by Ankur Nagpal, NA and PSA Easwaran. First line exactly नमस्ते नागराजेन्द्र नील नीलोत्पलद्युते. Site identifies verses 442 to 460 in its edition; Ghai translation numbers corresponding passage 351 to 369. Only first two space-separated words quoted, no claim to eighth-century surviving manuscript.

sources.title: Nilamata Purana, Ved Kumari Ghai translation, verses 301 to 400
sources.note: Verses 351 to 352 directly correspond to opening hymn; brief English rendering follows Ghai, omitting vocative Nila which follows the selected Sanskrit excerpt. Count together with Sanskrit and other Nilamata sources, deduplicating a passage cited to multiple witnesses.

sources.title: LACMA, The Infant Buddha Shakyamuni, M.87.233
sources.note: Museum object and curatorial research: Kashmir circa 800; brass with silver/copper inlay, height 14.6 cm. Sarada inscription translated by Gouriswar Bhattacharya; uncertain donor description retained. No invented original Sanskrit or reconstructed Sharada glyphs.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Vaikuntha Vishnu, 1991.301
sources.note: Museum object record and curatorial essay. Last quarter eighth century, Kashmir, stone, height 104.5 cm; fourth face on reverse and personified weapons. No known excavation findspot asserted.

sources.title: Martin Lerner, Panel from a Portable Shrine, in A Decade of Collecting 1984 to 1993
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum scholarly catalogue, printed page 47, object 1988.148.1. Eighth-century Kashmir ivory with color traces, 3.5 by 4.5 cm in this catalogue (current object page gives slightly different measurements). Tambourine identification, shrine reconstruction and Mara narrative explicitly tentative. Original indexed catalogue passage read.

sources.title: Martin Lerner, The Descent of the Buddha, Notable Acquisitions 1979 to 1980
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum scholarly catalogue, printed page 65, object 1979.287. Kashmir eighth century, ivory with paint traces, height 6.4 cm. Three steps, attendants and mother narrative; identities of attendants suggested rather than certain. Original indexed passage read; web full PDF exceeded size limit.

sources.title: District Baramulla, ParihasPora archaeological remains
sources.note: Official site directly read: eighth-century foundation by Lalitaditya, Buddhist stupa/monastery, Vishnu temples and large-stone construction; 1914 excavation. Do not reproduce erroneous Shankervarman capital association or inconsistent travel distances.

sources.title: District Anantnag, Martand Sun Temple
sources.note: Official heritage page directly read for dedication to Surya and surviving courtyard/carvings. Used only for observable remains, not exact construction dates or claims about origin of design.

sources.title: Oriental Numismatic Society, Journal 226 (2016), John Deyell research presentation
sources.note: Original numismatic society report of Reconsidering the so-called Kashmir and Karkota electrum dinaras. Indexed text directly read: traditional attribution questioned because find distribution and ruler names do not securely match. Describes an argument, not a settled blanket reattribution.

proposedOverrides.summary: Eighth-century Kashmir under the Karkota dynasty.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Eighth-century Karkota Kashmir; no association with later kashmir-and-ladakh.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Single imported world-700 polygon is approximate. Public map window is not founding/fall chronology. Royal chronology is scholarly reconstruction from later chronicle and outside evidence; avoid territorial maximum. Utpala succession is rounded in public prose to mid-ninth century; Witzel lists 856, while 855 is common elsewhere. No modern sovereignty inferred.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Modern Devanagari presentation of an attested Nilamata Sanskrit hymn, with translation; separate contemporary Sharada inscription discussed only in verified English translation.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceGaps: No secure household sanitation or medicine claim established for this exact century; omitted rather than imported from a later Kashmir period.
